The Gitea provider covers gitea.com and self-hosted Gitea instances. It uses the same implementation as the [Forgejo](/providers/forgejo) provider, so the Forgejo page applies here, apart from the default instance and the webhook headers. Refs from this provider have `forge: 'gitea'`.

## Authentication

The provider accepts an access token:

```ts
import { gitea } from 'forges/gitea'

const forge = gitea({
  auth: { type: 'token', token: process.env.GITEA_TOKEN! },
}).create()
```

Without `auth`, the provider makes anonymous public reads.

## Instance

The default instance is `https://gitea.com`. For a self-hosted instance, set `baseUrl` to the root of the instance. The provider appends `/api/v1`:

```ts
gitea({ baseUrl: 'https://gitea.example.com', auth })
```

`refreshCapabilities()` reads the instance version from `/version`.

These sections of the Forgejo page apply to Gitea:

## Webhooks

Set `webhookSecret` to the secret configured on the hook:

```ts
const forge = gitea({
  webhookSecret: process.env.GITEA_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
}).create()

const events = await forge.webhooks.ingest({
  headers: request.headers,
  body: await request.text(),
})
```

Gitea sends these headers with each delivery:

| Header | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Gitea-Signature` | The hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body |
| `X-Gitea-Event` | The event name |
| `X-Gitea-Delivery` | The delivery ID |

The Gitea provider doesn't read `X-Forgejo-*` headers.

A label delivery doesn't say which labels were added or removed. A changed label set becomes a `label` event with the `edited` action, and removing every label becomes one with the `unlabelled` action.

::contributing{title="Record Gitea fixtures" to="/contributing/record-fixtures"}
```sh
GITEA_TOKEN=... FIXTURE_GITEA_REPO=owner/repo FIXTURE_GITEA_PULL=1 \
pnpm record-fixtures gitea
```

To add an issue, set `FIXTURE_GITEA_ISSUE`. To record a self-hosted instance, set `GITEA_BASE_URL`.
::
